title: Virtual Schools
description: The lesson that listens instead of reading, and asks what is left of a school once the building is taken away: the four facts a report hands a listener - January 2006, Shan Jayran and her husband John Davies, an on-line high school called First College, twenty-two students now - and the two traps hidden in them, a husband named twice who is one man and a figure that counts the present and not the past; the timetable of a day that opens at nine on a connection and a chat in what it calls a school hall and closes at two on what it calls home time, the one line such a grid prints that no school with walls could print, the two expressions wearing inverted commas because they are on loan, the five hours from nine to two and the three classes the grid never counts aloud; the five new words with the definitions this lesson gives them - bullying, log on, appeal in the sense of what makes a thing attractive, texting, bustle - and the sixth definition that fits none of them; the difference between enrolling once and logging on every morning; the two young people the report follows, a boy of twelve with panic attacks and a bully behind him and a girl of thirteen afraid of speaking in front of a strict teacher, two reasons that name everything around a lesson and never the lesson itself; the benefits the report lets its pupils voice against the one drawback it states aloud, the side-effects of five hours in a chair; the five openings a role play is argued with and the hinge that three of them share, granting a point before turning it round; then the grammar the lesson turns on, do, does and did set in front of a verb that needed no auxiliary at all, the bare infinitive behind them, the person and the tense carried by the auxiliary alone, and the doubt such a sentence is almost always answering; and finally the two things the voice does - the letters English writes and no longer says, from the k of knee to the five silent letters that spell a past tense when they are read one after another, and the stress that moves from word to word until one sentence has answered four different questions

Teacher's Book - SKILLS For LIFE, CNP Tunisia 641404, KEY of Unit 2 lesson 3 (p. 25) - re-solved before use: the guide keys the gap-fill (January, husband, opened, on-line, 22), the five matched pairs and the definition left over (testing), the reasons of the two young people, the emphatic-form rule ("do+verb to emphasize meaning") and the seven words of the gapped paragraph, the fact that the ten printed words all contain silent letters and that the five underlined ones spell burnt; it gives NO key for the question on the journalist's opinion nor for the list of benefits and drawbacks, so this chapter states neither as a fact and builds both only from what the keyed material does say - the two reasons for enrolling, the completed paragraph, and the sentence "Sitting at a computer for 5 hours does have side-effects" quoted in the GRAMMAR FOCUS

Bornes de la R-7 du 2026-08-05 - le GRAMMAR REFERENCE (ADD-ONS p.261-271) ne contient AUCUNE entree sur la forme emphatique : le point de langue est traite au seul niveau que pose l'encadre MY GRAMMAR verbatim de la p.100 (do / does / did + infinitif sans to, exemple "He does work hard") et la cle du GRAMMAR FOCUS ("We use do+verb to emphasize meaning"). Aucun usage interrogatif, negatif ou lexical de do n'est enseigne ni teste ici. R-2 : aucun texte sous droits n'est reproduit - les documents sont decrits, les seules citations litterales sont l'exemple de l'encadre et la phrase support du GRAMMAR FOCUS. Ce que le chapitre AJOUTE aux encadres, declare ici pour que cette borne soit vraie : (1) la valeur "it is true that..." et le fait qu'une phrase emphatique repond presque toujours a un doute qui vient d'etre emis - lecture de la cle "We use do+verb to emphasize meaning" et du contexte de l'activite GRAMMAR FOCUS (le locuteur monte la voix sur does), enseignee comme lecture du point de langue et jamais donnee pour une regle imprimee ; (2) le blanc imprime p.98 dans "What you say is ....... but I still strongly believe..." est rempli par "true" dans les exercices, le cours gardant les points de suspension du manuel ; (3) les definitions de l'activite 3 p.97 sont normalisees en anglais courant ("connecting a computer to a system" pour "connect a computer system"), et l'une d'elles est tournee en gerondif comme les trois autres pour qu'aucun appariement ne se fasse sur la forme ; le sens keye p.25 reste intact ; (4) la chaine de lettres muettes "plumber, half, biscuits, autumn, listen" (blunt) du boss et la chaine "knee, autumn, friend, bustle" (knit) du cours sont construites par le chapitre au titre de la PRONUNCIATION FOCUS activite 3 p.99, qui demande justement d'en fabriquer une avec des mots a lettres muettes - la chaine du manuel (plumber, biscuits, harmful, autumn, listen, burnt) reste enseignee telle quelle ; (5) le r muet de harmful n'est vrai que dans la prononciation britannique du manuel, ce que le cours et le resume disent desormais ; (6) les repliques du jeu de role au-dela des cinq amorces imprimees sont ecrites par le chapitre - l'activite 7 p.98 demande precisement aux eleves de poursuivre la conversation avec leurs propres mots
